chunks: Yūnus, from Zur‘ah, from Samā‘ah, from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام:

For one leg there is half of the diyah. For the ear, there is half of the diyah if he cuts it from its root; and if he cuts its edge, then for it there is an equitable assessed value. For the nose, if it is cut off, the diyah is complete; and for the tongue, if it is cut off, the diyah is complete.

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: financial compensation due for bodily injury
key_terms.اللِّسَانِ: the tongue, for which full diyah is due if cut off
key_terms.الْأَنْفِ: the nose, for which full diyah is due if cut off
key_terms.الْأُذُنِ: the ear, as an injured body part with a specified diyah ruling
key_terms.طَرَفَهَا: its edge or tip, indicating partial injury
key_terms.قِيمَةُ عَدْلٍ: a fair assessed value determined justly
key_terms.كَامِلَةً: complete or full, indicating the full amount of diyah
key_terms.مِنْ أَصْلِهَا: from its root or base, meaning complete severance

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for cutting the ear, nose, tongue, or one leg in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states specific legal rulings for bodily injury compensation in cases involving the leg, ear, nose, and tongue. It distinguishes between complete severance and partial injury, assigning either a fixed diyah portion or an equitable assessed value according to the extent of damage.
